Answer: B
Reason: The frontal chest radiograph demonstrates enlarged central pulmonary arteries with peripheral pruning (oligemia), which are classic signs of pulmonary hypertension. The lateral view shows right ventricular enlargement (filling the retrosternal space), and this pattern is consistent with pulmonary hypertension secondary to a left-to-right shunt like an atrial septal defect.
